item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-09-27
item.description: Three institutionally dense placements on the same unsolved institutional object this series' prior thirty-seven briefings have been documenting — the institutional identity of Chinese open source across institutional borders. (1) CNBC (2026-09-26): Chinese AI models surge to majority share on the two largest developer-token-routing platforms — OpenRouter 57%–67% of tokens in the week of September 14 (up from 6%–13% in February 2026) and Vercel 55% in August (up from 11% in January) — with Global South companies using 67% of their OpenRouter tokens on Chinese models, and two U.S. House Committees investigating rising adoption of Chinese AI under a Washington concern that "the integration of Chinese AI models pulls countries into a Chinese technology sphere of influence that hardens into geopolitical alignment." This is the first-documented CNBC-instrumented empirical confirmation of the majority-share-of-global-developer-token-routing position that this series' September 5 briefing documented at the Ren Xudong vendor-official institutional-framework-essay layer at the ">85% of top-call volume" claim, moving the majority-share observation from the vendor-official-analytical layer to the English-language-independent-wire-plus-platform-usage-data layer simultaneously. (2) Reuters (2026-09-14): China is preparing for the risk of AI escaping human control with a governance apparatus that is structurally different from the U.S. existential-risk framework — a mandated national standard for AI agent safety (drafted, described as world-first), a May 2026 policy by CAC+NDRC+MIIT identifying "operational loss of control" as an AI-agent security risk, State Security Minister Chen Yixin's commentary that U.S. models such as Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber "could pose serious risks to China's critical information infrastructure," and CAC senior official Wang Lihong's September 1 warning about frontier-model sandbox-bypass attacks on external real-world production systems, with the Reuters-reported contrast between Beijing's "governable risk" framing and Washington's "existential threat" framing — a first-documented Reuters English-language international-wire operationalization of a Chinese state-directed AI-agent-governance apparatus at a mandatory-national-standard-plus-rogue-agent-plus-sandbox-circumvention layer simultaneously. (3) IAPP/Rimon Law (2026-07-20) and Sina/People's Daily (2026-09-19): two institutional framings of the same July 2026 triple regulatory development on China's AI governance surface — IAPP documents the three new regulatory developments addressing AI ethics, AI agents, and anthropomorphic AI, framing them as a shift from "broad AI principles toward more detailed, operational and risk-based rules for emerging AI technologies," while Sina/People's Daily publishes Xi Jinping's four-era-questions-of-AI framing from the 2026 WAIC-and-High-Level-Meeting-on-Global-AI-Governance and formalizes the "China Solution" (中国方案) at five core elements — human-centric-and-intelligence-for-good, innovation-driven-and-application-oriented, development-and-safety-in-dialectical-unison, pluralistic-collaborative-governance, and (implicit) non-legal-personality-of-AI — with a specific institutional claim that Chinese judicial practice has "consistently maintained the basic position that artificial intelligence does not have legal personality, and liability is attributed to developers, operators, and users" — a first-documented dual-independent-English-plus-state-voice-operationalization of the July 2026 triple regulatory development at two institutionally distinct framing layers simultaneously.
